method: PyMuPDF text layer (live text, not outlines) + vector paths. A Vectorworks dimension is two witness lines, a dimension line and two 9.0 pt 45-degree tick marks (0.576 pt wide). The drawn length is the distance between the two tick centres, which are the ends of the dimension line; witness lines start 4.5 pt from the measured point and run 9 pt past the dimension line.
units: sheet coordinates in PDF points, origin top-left, y down; 72 pt = 1 in

ska002_to_scene.note: A1.1 is drawn in the same sheet frame as SKA002 (same NW interior corner at X 1111.12, Y 365.86), so the same transform applies to its retained walls.

sheet_inconsistencies.detail: It runs from the west wall's interior face (X 1111.12) to the east face of the bedroom's east wall (X 1364.62), so it includes that 5" wall. The room is 13'-8" clear (X 1111.12 .. 1357.12). Every other room dimension on the sheet is face to face. The chain 3'-0" + 2'-6" + 2'-9" + 5" + 5'-0" + 5" = 14'-1" confirms it.

A 3'-0" window symbol sits in the old front wall at x 11.142 .. 14.142 (X 1307.62 .. 1361.62). On A1.1 that wall was exterior. On SKA002 the (N) office is behind it and the symbol runs 3 in into the office / foyer wall.

Drawn 6'-0 7/8" (109.31 pt) and 4'-7 1/16" (82.62 pt); the wall between them is drawn 7.57 pt. The three add up to exactly 11'-1" (199.50 pt). The W.I.C east wall and the W.I.C / bath wall are drawn 0.14 to 0.21 pt (about 1/8 in) out of square.

sheet_inconsistencies.what: every wall is drawn 5 in thick
sheet_inconsistencies.detail: Exterior and interior walls alike are 7.5 pt = 5 in between their face lines. No sheet states a wall thickness. Overall sizes therefore follow from clear sizes + 5 in walls: 39'-11" x 54'-4" (west side) / 53'-0" (east side) outside.
SKA002 has no overall width or depth string and no garage width (A1.1 gives 17'-7"). The overall 39'-11" comes from the chain + walls and agrees with SKA001 (52'-0" - 5'-7" - 6'-6").

"4 LEFT ELEVATION" shows the east facade (53'-0" long, chimney, garage side door, kitchen window); "2 RIGHT ELEVATION" shows the west facade (29'-1" main wall + garage beyond). Seen from the street the east side is on the right. Heights are not affected.
Drawn 6'-7 3/16" for 6'-7", 7'-11 31/32" for 8'-0", 1'-2 1/16" for 1'-2", 11 1/32" for 11", 4'-4 17/32" for 4'-4 1/2". Largest difference 0.205 in. The sheet is to scale.

A1.3 shows the existing house. The set has no elevation or section of the addition, so the new roof, the porch roof and the skylights have no heights on any sheet; SKA001 only gives the new roof outline, two ridge lines and "(N) 5/12".

sheet_inconsistencies.what: 23'-0" rear yard dimension is shifted 2 in
sheet_inconsistencies.detail: Both of its ends sit 2.25 pt north of the lines it measures (rear property line Y 108.33, rear wall face Y 418.83). Its length is exactly the distance between those lines, so the value is right.
It runs from the old front wall of the main house to the (E) fence line, which meets the garage 2 in behind its front face. The garage projects 23'-11" (A1.1 by scaling: Y 881.86 .. 1312.36).
20% of 52 ft is 10.4 ft = 10'-4 13/16"; the sheet rounds it to 10'-5". The conclusion (12'-1" > 10'-5") holds either way.

text_layer_check: All 120 dimension strings are live text in the PDF text layer (fonts with a Unicode map; none outlined). Every dimension object found in the vector geometry (240 tick marks = 120 dimensions) has exactly one text and no dimension text is left over; the only other size texts are the 25 level labels on A1.3 and the notes listed under size_labels_that_are_not_dimension_objects. They were also compared by eye with renderings of the sheets (all 39 of SKA002 on enlarged crops; A1.1 on the page overview and two enlarged crops; the other sheets on page overviews) and agree.
